title: The Critical Line
chapters: The critical strip, the exact target, and the role of Dirichlet characters.
Prime powers and the Mellin transform
Follow one prime power from an Euler product to a residue.
Factorials, local coordinates, and the cost of mixed derivatives.
From the global theta function to an integral jet
Follow an integral expansion through torsion translation and a change of local frame.
Lattices and the arithmetic main term
Transporting a bound through metrics, ranks, and normalized maps.
Theta lifts, local factors and the Galois input
Follow the pair used for the Galois construction and compute the local factors that keep an iterated lift nonzero.
Character averaging and the costs that a square-root estimate must absorb.
How class groups, cyclotomic descent and signed character estimates supply one arithmetic window.
How derivatives concentrated on distant intervals exclude a pole.
Removing Euler factors, exchanging characters, and returning to zeta.
glossary: A compatible list of local entries, one in each completion of a number field, integral at all but finitely many finite places. The diagonal embedding sends one field element to its value in every completion.
A property holds almost everywhere if the set where it fails has measure zero. Two functions in L² can differ on such a set and still represent the same vector.
An extension agreeing with a given analytic function on its original domain. Agreement on an open subset determines the continuation on a connected domain.
The characters of a finite abelian group that are identically one on a specified subgroup. Subgroup averaging selects exactly these characters.
For t in a commutative ring, Ann(t) is the ideal of all x with tx = 0. In a ring containing η with η² = 0, this ideal can contain η itself.
The homomorphism from integer combinations of vertices to the integers that sends each vertex to one. Its kernel consists of the zero-dimensional cycles that the edges must fill.
A function on an adelic group that descends under its rational subgroup and satisfies the prescribed regularity and other conditions. Square-integrability on the quotient matters for the lifts here.
A finite linear combination of ordered words in a group. Its boundary takes alternating faces obtained by omitting an end entry or multiplying neighboring entries.
A weighted finite sum of Bernoulli polynomial values at fractions of the conductor. The minus estimate clears its denominators and uses the same algebraic integer at every coefficient prime.

In the coefficient sequence for reduction modulo q, lift a cycle to an integral chain. Its boundary is a multiple of q. Dividing that boundary by q gives a class one degree lower, killed by q. This map distinguishes the two torsion orders in the cycle count.
A homomorphism from a finite group to nonzero complex numbers. A Dirichlet character extends by zero off the units modulo N.
Fractional ideals of the number field K modulo principal fractional ideals. The quotient Cl(K)/ℓCl(K) measures the number of independent characters of order ℓ.
A number field that is a totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real field. Complex conjugation interchanges the two embeddings over any real place of the base.
A function c satisfying c(gh)=c(g)+g·c(h). Its class in degree one identifies functions differing by g↦g·a−a. Local conditions impose restrictions on these classes.
A linear functional that vanishes on boundaries. For the residue test, consecutive pairs contribute carries and the last entry contributes an additive index.
For two maps with a common source and target, a point of the source at which their values agree. For the identity map paired with a self-map, these are the fixed points of the self-map.
Given an operator g on a module M, the quotient M/(g−1)M identifies each element with its translate under g. The quotient by gᵈ−1 maps onto it because gᵈ−1 is divisible by g−1.
The least divisor of the modulus from which a Dirichlet character is induced. A primitive character has conductor equal to its modulus.
The volume of a fundamental parallelepiped of a lattice in its real span with the chosen metric.
The volume of one fundamental parallelepiped, measured in the chosen ambient coordinates. In the complex plane the lattice generated by α and iα has covolume |α|².
The region 0 < Re s < 1. Here s = σ+it; σ = ½ is the critical line.
A stage in a tower formed by adjoining roots of unity. In the ℓ-adic tower here, layer m has relative degree ℓᵐ over the chosen base field.
A ring in which each nonzero element has the form uπⁿ for a unit u, a fixed uniformizer π and a nonnegative integer n. This exponent measures divisibility. For ℤℓ one can take π=ℓ.
For subgroups Γ and K of a group, the double coset of h consists of the products γhk with γ in Γ and k in K. Grouping an integral by these classes preserves the measure of each class.

An integral obtained by placing two copies of a unitary group in a larger group and pairing a section there with matrix coefficients on the original copies. Its local factors determine the partial L-function in the theta norm.

A pair of full local lattices can be put into diagonal form by integral changes of bases. The integer exponents of a uniformizer classify their relative position. Their sum gives the determinant valuation and the sum of their absolute values gives the degree in the split-place series.
The limit of 1+1/2+⋯+1/n − log n; it is the constant Laurent coefficient of ζ at 1.

In a Galois extension the field norm multiplies all conjugates of an element. The ideal norm sends a prime above a base prime to the power of the base prime given by the relative residue degree. For a principal ideal these two constructions agree.
The positive constant in Schur orthogonality for a discrete series and a chosen Haar measure. For a unit vector v it satisfies ∫|⟨v,σ(g)v⟩|² dg = 1/dσ.
A group law in power series at the identity and a change of coordinate taking that law to addition.
Frame of a regular Gram fibre
An ordered list of independent vectors whose matrix of mutual Hermitian pairings is nonsingular. Its length can be smaller than the ambient dimension.
Inertia is the subgroup of a local Galois group acting trivially on the residue field. A Frobenius class acts there by raising to the residue-field size.
For an operator T and a scalar λ, this is the space of vectors killed by some power of T − λ. Its dimension counts the whole nilpotent chain at λ, including vectors that are not eigenvectors.
For a positive definite lattice, sum 1/|Aut(L)| over one representative of each isometry class in its genus. A weighted average of a count divides the corresponding weighted sum by this mass.
The full lattices in a fixed rational Hermitian space that are isometric to a given lattice at every finite place. A genus may contain several global isometry classes.
The matrix of pairwise inner products of a list of vectors. Its diagonal records squared lengths. If the vectors are columns of M in orthonormal coordinates, the Gram matrix is M* M.
A translation-invariant measure on a locally compact group. Its normalization matters when comparing the two sides of the Petersson identity.
An operator formed by summing translates indexed by the cosets in a double coset. The operator in the invariant-period comparison divides by the number of cosets, so it fixes constants.

A cycle is a chain with zero boundary, and its homology class records it up to addition of boundaries. A cohomology class tests cycles by a cocycle, which vanishes on boundaries. Torsion counts and bounds on the dimension over the reals give different information.
The product of the normalized local absolute values of an invertible adèle. The product formula makes it one on each nonzero field element.
A surjective homomorphism of abelian varieties with finite kernel. Its degree counts the rank of the kernel group scheme.
A nested sequence of subspaces on which every two vectors have Hermitian pairing zero. Its successive increases in dimension are its rank jumps.

For two multiplicative characters of a finite field, extended by zero at zero, sum χ(x)φ(1−x) over the field. In the nondegenerate cyclotomic case the product with the inverse-character sum is the size of the field.
An identification that assigns a specified torsion point to each label at a chosen level. Permuting the torsion points can change the marking.
An eigenvalue chosen by the positive line of the period datum. Its place in the root list specifies which determinant factors carry the form-degree variable.
The scalar formed by translating one vector by a group element and pairing it with a second vector. When the vectors coincide, its value at the identity is their squared norm.
The ℤℓ-module of finite integral linear combinations of the group matrices. It contains the identity, and left multiplication by the group preserves it.
Here the integral from 1 to infinity against x^(−s−1) dx. Under x=eᵘ it becomes a Laplace transform.
Number of simple quotients in a composition series. For a finite ℤℓ-module of order ℓᵈ the length is d. Its minimum number of generators can be smaller.

A short Dirichlet polynomial chosen to cancel the early coefficients of a product with the L-series. Here its weights are μ(d)χ(d), where μ is the Möbius function. A zero forces the product of the two truncated sums to be small.

An identification of tangent spaces used to compare a form at different points. In the cone of positive Hermitian matrices, the action carrying the identity to a point pulls the form back to a tensor at the identity.
At an isolated zero ρ, the integer m≥1 such that L(s)=(s−ρ)ᵐh(s) with h holomorphic and h(ρ)≠0. The balance chapter also uses m for a chain length.
An ordered tuple of cover labels is allowed when their sets share a witness. Deleting a label gives a face. Alternating deletion gives the boundary on integer combinations of tuples.
A collection of smooth nonnegative weights that add to one, with only finitely many nonzero in a neighborhood of each point. Here the weights index translates by the arithmetic group.

An integral of an automorphic function over a specified quotient, often after restricting the function to a subgroup or pairing it with a second function. The bottom period here restricts a core function to the row group and integrates their product.
The integral of the product of an automorphic function and the complex conjugate of another on the automorphic quotient, with the chosen measure. On the diagonal it gives a squared norm.

A sum of translates of a test function over a discrete group or a coset space. The sum used to separate a row has an identity contribution large enough to dominate the sum of the other contributions after unfolding its period.
The residue is the coefficient of (s−ρ)⁻¹ in a Laurent expansion. A simple pole has a nonzero residue and no higher-order singular terms.
The number max(u,0). In a ramp it cuts off the sum; in the window estimate it keeps the side controlled by the hypothesis.
A module that is a direct summand of a free module. A relation solved in the free module can be projected back to the summand.
The multiplicity of a prime in the extended prime ideal. It enters the weighting of the finite-place contributions to divisibility.
The volume spanned by logarithms of a basis of free units after deleting one place coordinate. The complex coordinates use log |z|². In a field with unit rank zero this volume is one.
For a given generic cover, take all functions on the cover integral over each affine open of the base. Their rings define the normal model used for the source of the correspondence.
The degree of an extension of residue fields. In an unramified quadratic extension, a split base prime has two primes of residue degree one. An inert prime has one of degree two.
A family of local coordinates integral at all but finitely many finite places. For the multiplicative group, both a coordinate and its inverse must be integral there.
A chosen trivialization on a specified subscheme, often the zero section of a group scheme. On a square the polarization bundle here has a trivialization on each zero axis.

The unramified eigenvalue data that encode the action of the spherical Hecke operators at one place. The normalization used here specifies their powers of the residue-field size in the local Euler factors.
The saturation of Λ in E is the set of x in E such that kx lies in Λ for some nonzero integer k. Modulo Λ it gives exactly the torsion subgroup of E/Λ.
The symmetric polynomial attached to a partition. Its product with the Vandermonde determinant is the alternant with row exponents shifted by that partition.
A smooth function on a real vector space whose derivatives of every order decay faster than every inverse power of the norm. A Gaussian is an example.
A full lattice L consisting exactly of the vectors whose Hermitian pairings with L are integral. This condition makes integral adjoints available in the construction of a frame.
A direct sum of irreducible representations. One can compare multiplicities constituent by constituent once an isomorphism of the global representations has been established.
The subgroup of degree-one Galois cohomology classes whose restrictions at the specified places vanish. Its module length enters the cohomological window bound.
Homology with an induced coefficient module can be computed in the subgroup. Here the module of functions on a finite cyclic quotient turns a homology calculation for G into one for the kernel.
The subgroup preserving a maximal isotropic subspace in the doubled Hermitian space. Its rational cosets index the Eisenstein series used to identify the normalized theta mean.
The signs of a unit at all real embeddings. Recording a negative value as one and a positive value as zero turns multiplication of units into addition of bit vectors.
An invertible linear map that multiplies a Hermitian form by a single nonzero scalar. It sends the sphere of one length to the sphere of the scaled length.
For a Euclidean lattice of positive rank, its Arakelov slope is the negative log of its covolume divided by its rank. Extremal slopes measure sublattices and quotients.
At a good finite place the vectors are fixed by the specified maximal compact subgroup. This invariance permits the local integral to be evaluated by Hecke eigenvalues.
An ordered list of vectors vᵢ with specified linear functionals λᵢ satisfying λᵢ(vⱼ)=1 when i=j and 0 otherwise. Deleting one pair gives a shorter sequence.

The subgroup of symmetries that take an object to itself. In the arithmetic face count a finite stabilizer acts faithfully on a finite set of shortest vectors. Its order contributes to the bound for integral homology.
An element of a group ring acting on ideal classes in cyclotomic arithmetic. Its annihilation property supplies a relation on a quotient of the class group in the tower argument.

For a lattice in a Euclidean space, the jth successive minimum is the least radius of a ball about zero containing j real-linearly independent lattice vectors. In the number-field row argument, independence over the field requires taking the radii in blocks.
For a kernel K(x,y) and a fixed source point x, the function y ↦ K(x,y) on the target. Its square-integral as x varies controls the change of integration order in the theta pairing.
A change in a Galois action by a power of the cyclotomic character, which records the action on roots of unity. Its exponent matters in a local restriction kernel.
An integral operator with a theta kernel carrying an automorphic function between spaces for two groups.
The region of positive Hermitian forms where both the primal and dual lattice minima are at least a fixed positive constant. A compact set meets every arithmetic orbit in this region.

For a finite separable extension, bases (uᵢ) and (vⱼ) are trace-dual when Tr(uᵢvⱼ) is 1 for i=j and 0 otherwise. Then x=∑ᵢ Tr(xuᵢ)vᵢ. Clearing both bases at once produces the split residue calculation.
For a matrix X and a group representation r, the measurement tr(Xr(g)). Varying g can detect coordinates invisible to tr(X) itself.
The exponent of p in a nonzero rational number, extended by vₚ(0)=+∞. The normalized p-adic absolute value is p to the power −vₚ.
Λ(pʲ)=log p for a prime p and integer j≥1; its value at every other positive integer is zero.

A Fourier coefficient obtained by integrating along a unipotent matrix variable against an additive character. In the Siegel–Weil calculation, a nonsingular Hermitian matrix specifies the character. At the special parameter the coefficient reads the density of tuples with that Gram matrix.
An interval [Y,Y¹⁺ᵟ] with δ>0; in logarithmic coordinates its endpoints are U=log Y and (1+δ)U.
Largest dimension of a subspace on which the entire Hermitian pairing vanishes. It determines which convergence hypothesis is required for the doubled theta integral.
